For a course-unit field, the accepted operational window is 1 through 60 credits; it is a policy and workload window, not the observed minimum and maximum in a particular catalog extract. A wrong generalization is to infer that a course with 30 credits must be a semester course or that every institution uses ECTS-sized credits.","wrong_generalization":"The largest sampled credit value defines the allowed maximum, or ECTS credits are interchangeable with all local credit-hour systems.","semantic_type":"academic_credit_quantity","positives":["5","30","60"],"near_misses":["0","61","005"],"ambiguity_types":["policy_window_vs_sample_range","credit_system_confusion","integer_width"],"program":{"op":"int","min":1,"max":60,"lo":1,"hi":2},"neighbors":[{"concept":"US semester credit hour","relation":"different workload and contact-time convention"},{"concept":"Carnegie unit","relation":"secondary-school instructional-time measure"}]},{"domain":"education","concept":"Transcript degree-conferral month abbreviation","description":"Many academic transcript and degree-conferral exports use an uppercase three-letter calendar-month abbreviation for the month in which a credential is conferred. A wrong generalization is to interpret this token as a term name, an enrollment month, or a free-text month field.","wrong_generalization":"Any uppercase three-letter word is a valid conferral month, or the month token identifies an academic term.","semantic_type":"credential_conferral_month","positives":["MAY","JUN","DEC"],"near_misses":["May","APRIL","FAL"],"ambiguity_types":["month_vs_academic_term","case_significance","closed_vocabulary"],"program":{"op":"lex","name":"month_abbr_upper"},"neighbors":[{"concept":"Academic term code","relation":"term labels such as FALL or SPRING are not calendar months"},{"concept":"Graduation date","relation":"full date field rather than a month-only token"}]},{"domain":"education","concept":"Syllabus document revision identifier","description":"Institutional course-syllabus document control commonly labels a base syllabus year and may append an R-number revision suffix, for example SYL-2024-R2. A wrong generalization is to require a revision suffix on every syllabus or to treat R2 as a second course section.","wrong_generalization":"Every syllabus identifier must include a revision number, or the revision number is an academic-section identifier.","semantic_type":"curriculum_document_revision_identifier","positives":["SYL-2024","SYL-2024-R2","SYL-2030-R12"],"near_misses":["SYL2024","SYL-2024-R0","SYL-2024-REV2"],"ambiguity_types":["optional_component","revision_vs_section","document_control_vs_catalog_identity"],"program":{"op":"seq","children":[{"op":"lit","text":"SYL-"},{"op":"int","min":2000,"max":2099,"lo":4,"hi":4},{"op":"opt","child":{"op":"seq","children":[{"op":"lit","text":"-R"},{"op":"int","min":1,"max":99,"lo":1,"hi":2}]}}]},"neighbors":[{"concept":"Course catalog number","relation":"academic offering identifier rather than document revision"},{"concept":"Learning management system version","relation":"platform content version rather than controlled syllabus revision"}]},{"domain":"education","concept":"Course learning outcome tag list","description":"Course learning outcomes are often tagged as CLO-1, CLO-2, and so on; catalog and accreditation exports may serialize multiple tags as a semicolon-delimited list.
